key_insight: Ms-LegONet learns reusable, coefficient-dependent local finite-element spaces that compose into larger solvers with localized error bounds.
engineering_relevance: It accelerates heterogeneous elliptic simulations while allowing changes in coefficient layouts, loads, boundary data and domain size without retraining within the trained coefficient class.
method: Train one network per spatial dimension on local coefficient patches and patch-level harmonic responses, without global training solves.
Predict zero-boundary spaces, then compute multiscale basis functions through local Galerkin harmonic extensions with shared interface traces.
Assemble larger blocks by recursive static condensation and attribute approximation error to individual primitives using a localized Céa bound.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 4–150× lower L² errors than baselines at equal unknowns on 2D mosaics, 1.6–2.3× speedups over fine-grid direct solves in 2D, and 30–900× speedups for 3D many-query port responses.
watch_item: Reuse is restricted to the trained coefficient class; accuracy for out-of-distribution material patterns requires separate validation.
paper_title: Multiscale LegONet: Learning Coefficient-Dependent Local Spaces for Composable Multiscale Finite Elements with Localized Error Bounds
